drug_class: Gene therapy / Topical biological agent (herpes simplex virus type 1 vector-based gene therapy)
purpose: This medication is used to treat a rare, serious skin condition called dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB), which causes very fragile skin that blisters and wounds easily. It is applied directly to wounds to help them heal. It works for people who have a specific gene mutation that causes this condition.
how_it_works: Your skin blisters because it is missing a working copy of a gene that makes a protein called collagen VII, which normally holds skin layers together. This medicine uses a modified, harmless virus to deliver a working copy of that gene directly into your skin cells when applied to wounds. Once inside, your skin cells can start making the collagen VII protein they need, helping wounds close and heal better.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include itching, chills, redness or irritation at the site where the medicine is applied, and a feeling similar to having a cold or mild flu. Some people may also notice skin blisters or mild pain near the treated area.
warnings: This medicine contains a modified virus, so you should tell your doctor if you or anyone in your household is pregnant, trying to get pregnant, or has a weakened immune system. The virus can be found in the wound dressing and on treated skin, so used dressings must be disposed of carefully and caregivers should wear gloves. Avoid letting untreated people come into close contact with the treated wound or used bandages. Keep this medication away from eyes and mucous membranes.
typical_dosing: This medicine is applied directly to your wounds by a healthcare provider or trained caregiver once a week. The amount used depends on the size of the wound being treated. Your doctor or care team will show you exactly how to apply it safely and how to handle and dispose of the used dressings properly.
